key_insight: The bits needed to preserve fine-tuned behavior depend on the dataset–base-model pair, not simply adapter rank, parameter count, or reconstruction error.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate compressed LoRA adapters after reloading them into the target frozen model, since smaller adapters can preserve useful behavior and sometimes reduce corruption-induced damage.
method: Define behavioral rate R* as the smallest serialized adapter size retaining a fixed fraction of held-out fine-tuning gain.
Compare compression rates across training content and frozen base models at fixed optimization budgets.
Analyze data-measured correction spectra and test compression on deliberately corrupted fine-tunes.
evidence_signal: On GSM8K with Qwen2.5-7B, compression raised a corrupted adapter’s accuracy from 23.7% to 82.9%, versus 77.6% for the frozen base; on harder math, the compressed corrupted adapter retained 97% of base accuracy versus 44% for a clean fine-tune.
watch_item: Behavioral rate is receiver- and evaluation-dependent, so compression settings and corruption-recovery gains require validation for each target model and task.
paper_title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information
